newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Thousands celebrate anniversary of Fatima visions.
newsitem.headline: Thousands celebrate anniversary of Fatima visions.

text.p: Tens of thousands of pilgrims gathered at the Roman Catholic shrine at Fatima in Portugal on Sunday to celebrate the 79th anniversary of what they believe to be the apparition of the Virgin Mary there.

During Sunday's ceremonies, Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, head of the Vatican's Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, blessed a statue of Virgin before it left on a nine-month tour of Russia, Siberia and Kazakhstan.

According to Church sources, it will be the first time that a statue of the Virgin has made such a visit to the former Soviet Union. Russian Catholic Church officials travelled to Fatima to accompany the statue on its journey.
The annual celebration, which has a strong following in Catholic Portugal, particularly in rural areas, attracts hundreds of pilgrims from Europe and North America.

Many Catholics make the pilgrimage to honour promises made to the Virgin Mary, who they believe appeared to three peasant children at Fatima on a number of occasions between May 13 and October 13, 1917.
Sister Lucia de Jesus dos Santos is the only one of the three visionaries still alive. Ratzinger will meet her on Monday at her Carmelite convent in the nearby city of Coimbra.
Lucia, now 89, and two cousins said that the Virgin had made several prophesies to them.
The best known, made a few months before the Bolshevik Revolution, was that Russia would spread "errors" through the world, but would eventually be converted.

Pope John Paul paid a visit to the shrine, 130 km (80 miles) north of Lisbon, in 1991 to give thanks to the Virgin of Fatima for the dramatic changes in Eastern Europe and for his having survived an assassination attempt in 1981.
The Pope was shot and wounded by Turkish gunman Ali Agca in Rome on May 13, 1981. He attributes his survival to divine intervention by the Virgin of Fatima, on whose feast day the attack occurred.
